title: Christa Pike’s Death Sentence Takes an Unexpected Turn in Tennessee
subheadline: Pike was scheduled to become the first woman executed by Tennessee in more than 200 years, but the state stopped the procedure after she remained alive following two doses of lethal-injection drugs.
bodyContent:
Christa Pike’s scheduled execution in Tennessee took an unexpected turn Wednesday night after the state’s attempt to carry out her lethal injection was halted and she was taken to a medical facility. 

Pike, 50, had been scheduled to become the first woman executed by Tennessee in more than 200 years. She was convicted of the 1995 killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer when Pike was 18.

The execution itself had already been delayed earlier Wednesday. The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit issued a temporary stay about an hour before the scheduled execution while considering whether claims about Pike’s childhood sexual abuse had received proper consideration. The U.S. Supreme Court later overturned that stay, allowing Tennessee to proceed.

After the Supreme Court ruling, prison officials resumed preparations at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville. Pike was administered two doses of the drug used in Tennessee’s lethal-injection protocol, according to court filings from her attorneys.

Media witnesses reported that Pike remained alive after the second dose. Her attorneys subsequently filed an emergency motion seeking to halt the execution, while the Tennessee Department of Correction confirmed that Pike had been transported to an off-site medical facility. Officials did not initially provide details about her condition.

title: ‘By Any Means’ Review: Mark Wahlberg’s Gangster for a Good Cause
subheadline: The actor stars alongside Yahya Abdul-Mateen II as a mob hitman enlisted by the FBI to help investigate a racist murder in 1960s Mississippi in this bare-knuckle historical drama.
cardSummary: “By Any Means” suggests it takes a dirty man to clean up a historically and culturally entrenched mess. We’re in 1966 Mississippi, where a straitlaced black FBI...
bodyContent:
“By Any Means” suggests it takes a dirty man to clean up a historically and culturally entrenched mess. We’re in 1966 Mississippi, where a straitlaced black FBI agent (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II) and a career criminal (Mark Wahlberg) become unlikely partners in an effort to solve a racist murder. Welcome to a race-swapped “48 Hrs.” with a heart of righteous fury.  

Civil-rights dramas tend to be preachy and self-congratulatory, painting halos on the white saviors and the black victims, but the rousing “By Any Means” takes a literally punchy approach. It filters the trauma of race-based suffering through a genre piece about busting heads. Setting out to rebut the sanctimony of, say, “To Kill a Mockingbird,” with its holy glow, the feature directed by Elegance Bratton (“The Inspection”) has more of a “Dirty Harry” vibe. In a system corrupted by racism, justice is sometimes unattainable. If they mess with you, notes Mr. Wahlberg’s character, you’re allowed to mess with them, except he uses a different verb than “mess.”

title: A ‘Useless Master’s’ in New York Becomes a Viral Wealth Fantasy
subheadline: A viral post imagining life with enough family wealth to study in New York has sparked conversations about education, privilege, humanities degrees and the freedom to choose a path without immediate financial pressure.
cardSummary: What would you study if you never had to worry about whether your degree would lead to a high-paying job? That question is at the center of a viral post from so...
bodyContent:
What would you study if you never had to worry about whether your degree would lead to a high-paying job? That question is at the center of a viral post from social media user Carra, who wrote that if she had generational wealth, she would “definitely be doing some useless master's in New York.” The post quickly drew thousands of reactions online.

The joke opened the door to an oddly specific fantasy of wealthy New York life. Replies imagined living in Manhattan, attending graduate school, studying creative writing or niche humanities subjects and spending years in the city for the experience rather than for a conventional career payoff.

For many commenters, the appeal was less about the degree itself and more about the freedom surrounding it. With family wealth covering tuition, rent and everyday expenses, graduate school could become a way to meet people, explore an intellectual interest or simply experience New York without the same pressure to turn education into immediate income.

Others pushed back on the fantasy. Some argued that people with substantial generational wealth might not need another degree at all, while others pointed out that being able to pursue an expensive graduate program without worrying about employment is itself a form of privilege.

title: $10 Million Raised, Then $10 Million More: Olivia Rodrigo's Festival Makes a Huge Impact
subheadline: The singer's Daisy Chain Fields festival raised $10 million for organizations supporting women and girls, including reproductive health groups, before Melinda French Gates matched the amount and pushed the total to $20 million.
bodyContent:
Olivia Rodrigo's new music festival became much more than a celebration of female artists.

It became a multimillion-dollar fundraiser for women and girls.

Rodrigo announced that her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival raised $10 million for 10 nonprofit organizations, including groups supporting reproductive health and rights, maternal health, survivors of gender-based violence and economic justice. The announcement came as advocates have raised concerns about changes to federal funding and policies affecting reproductive healthcare in the United States.

But the story did not end there.

Before it ever reappears as something you would like to swim in, the majority of hot springs start out as perfectly normal rain or groundwater that seeps through fissures and faults in the Earth's crust, often for years.

title: Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland Unite Around Self Determination
subheadline: The leaders of the Scottish National Party, Plaid Cymru and Sinn Féin signed a joint agreement calling for self-determination and closer ties with the European Union.
cardSummary: Leaders from Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have joined forces in a new push for constitutional change, declaring that their nations have the right to det...
bodyContent:
Leaders from Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have joined forces in a new push for constitutional change, declaring that their nations have the right to determine their own futures and saying they see those futures within the European Union.

The agreement was signed in Cardiff on Sept. 14 by John Swinney of Scotland’s Scottish National Party, Rhun ap Iorwerth of Wales’ Plaid Cymru and Michelle O’Neill of Northern Ireland’s Sinn Féin, alongside Sinn Féin president Mary Lou McDonald. The leaders met in their political-party roles rather than as representatives of their governments.

The memorandum states that “our nations have the right to self-determination” and argues that no Westminster government should prevent people in Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland from deciding their political future. It also declares, “The future of our nations belongs in the European Union.”

The three parties have different constitutional goals. The SNP supports Scottish independence, Plaid Cymru supports Welsh independence, while Sinn Féin campaigns for Northern Ireland to leave the United Kingdom and join a united Ireland. Their positions also differ over when and how votes on constitutional change should take place.

Scotland has already held an independence referendum. In 2014, voters rejected independence by 55.3% to 44.7%, with Scotland remaining part of the United Kingdom. Swinney has called for another referendum, while the UK government has opposed an immediate new vote.

title: Why Did Typhoon Dujuan Cause So Much Damage in Japan?
subheadline: Typhoon Dujuan had departed from Japan, but heavy rainfall, landslides and flooding had resulted in a trail of devastation in the region near Tokyo
cardSummary: The storm also wreaked havoc. Roads were inundated, railway services were halted and houses were in danger of being damaged. Many people were left stranded when...
bodyContent:
The storm also wreaked havoc. Roads were inundated, railway services were halted and houses were in danger of being damaged. Many people were left stranded when Japan Airlines cancelled 135 flights and All Nippon Airways cancelled 140.
But how can a storm moving away cause such problems?
The greatest threat was rainfall. Dujuan dumped tremendous amounts of water over eastern Japan. In the island of Oshima, just south of Tokyo, over 800 millimetres of rain fell in 48 hours, twice the monthly rainfall for the island!
In this scenario, the ground can become saturated and unstable when so much rain falls in a brief time period. Landslides can occur and rivers can surge quickly, flooding surrounding towns and cities. A mudslide in the Japanese port of Yokosuka inundated a house, killing a woman in her 60s. Search and rescue teams were also combing through debris for any missing persons.
The threat from the storm was not the only one. Even as Dujuan turned east-northeast into the Pacific, the already swollen rivers and saturated ground posed threats. Heavy rains may persist until the typhoon passed, Japan's weather agency said.
Typhoons are a common occurrence in Japan, and each one might be hazardous in a different way due to the amount of rainfall. The image demonstrates that a tropical cyclone can still cause significant flooding and landslides even if it doesn't directly pass over the location.
For communities near rivers and steep slopes, the most perilous time of a storm can occur after a community experiences the strongest winds.

title: Radio signals have been detected directly from an exoplanet.
subheadline: Astronomers have uncovered radio waves they claim can be directly linked to a planet outside our Solar System for the first time, which will provide a new means for astronomers to explore worlds beyond the Sun's influence
cardSummary: A group of astronomers at the Center for Astrophysics, Harvard & Smithsonian and the University of Oregon has announced the first radio waves ever detected dire...
bodyContent:
A group of astronomers at the Center for Astrophysics, Harvard & Smithsonian and the University of Oregon has announced the first radio waves ever detected directly from an exoplanet. The planet, Beta Pictoris b, is a huge gas giant located about 63 light years from Earth.
The researchers used the MeerKAT radio telescope in South Africa to detect radio waves coming from the planet. Radio activity has been observed in systems with exoplanets before, but scientists were not able to rule out that the radio activity was originating in the exoplanet or from the host star. This time, the researchers could identify the emission, unit by unit, to the planet Beta Pictoris b.
What is causing the signal?
The radio waves seem to be linked with auroral activity, like the northern and southern lights on Earth.
What can a radio signal tell scientists about a planet that they can't visit?
Auroras are formed when particles with electrical charges interact with a planet's magnetic field. These interactions can also generate radio waves. The more the researchers know about the emission, the more they will be able to learn about the strength of the magnetic field of the planet.
The study indicates that the magnetic field of Beta Pictoris b is very strong, at least 1000 times stronger than Earth's. This planet is about 10 times bigger than Jupiter.
Eventually, the finding might help scientists understand how planets protect their own atmospheres and how they interact with the powerful wind that results from a planet's own star.
Yet this is not proof of an alien civilisation: even the catchy term 'radio signals from an exoplanet' must be taken with a pinch of salt. The emission is a natural phenomenon that is linked to the magnetic environment of the planet.
Rather, it provides astronomers with something far more useful: a new approach to the study of the invisible magnetic properties of worlds many light years distant.

Weinstein, 74, appeared in a Manhattan courtroom in a wheelchair for the sentencing. Prosecutors had asked for 20 years, while his defense requested a nine-year sentence, citing his age and health problems.

Haley addressed the court before the sentence was announced, describing the lasting effects of the assault and the years of legal proceedings that followed. She said the experience had affected her sense of safety and described the consequences as continuing long after the 2006 incident.

Weinstein expressed regret for the pain Haley said she experienced but continued to maintain his innocence regarding the assault. He asked the judge for mercy and said he was not a perfect person but had made mistakes.

The latest sentence follows a complicated legal history. Weinstein was originally convicted in New York in 2020 and sentenced to 23 years after being found guilty of sexually assaulting Haley and raping aspiring actress Jessica Mann. New York's highest court overturned those convictions in 2024, ruling that the original trial had been unfair because of testimony concerning allegations that were not part of the charges.

title: Why Do We Procrastinate Even When We know Better?
subheadline: You are aware that the deadline is nearing and that the work must be completed. Suddenly, checking your phone, watching a video or doing something completely different becomes much easier. Why is it that we love to put things off?
cardSummary: Procrastination is frequently viewed as laziness, but there is more to the psychology of procrastination. It is defined by researchers as needlessly postponing ...
bodyContent:
Procrastination is frequently viewed as laziness, but there is more to the psychology of procrastination. It is defined by researchers as needlessly postponing a desired action when there is a potential for harm. Research is becoming more and more associated with the link between procrastination and emotion regulation. Sometimes, we don't want to do something because we don't want the feeling we get from the result rather than the action itself.

Think of arriving at an assignment and being overwhelmed by it. You don't start, instead you look at social media. This is a short-term discomfort that lasts for a few minutes. That temporary relief can reinforce the habit, making it easier to repeat the behaviour later.

Even clues could be found within the brain. An MRI study published in Psychological Science in 2018 identified the amygdala as a brain area that is associated with procrastination. The people with less action control had a larger amygdala and weaker links between the amygdala and the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, which is part of the brain that controls actions.

But that doesn't mean that a bigger amygdala leads to procrastination. The study found an association, but not a direct cause, and more research is required to understand the mechanisms in the brain, researchers said.

title: Doctors, Hospitals Struggle to Keep Up With Ebola’s Spread

bodyContent:
NAIROBI, Kenya—The fast-spreading Ebola virus is overwhelming creaking hospitals and clinics in the Democratic Republic of Congo, dimming hopes for quick containment of what is already the third-largest outbreak of the killer disease in history.

With at least 750 suspected cases and an official death count of 177 as of this weekend—the actual toll is likely higher—patients are being treated in ordinary wards because of a lack of dedicated Ebola treatment centers in the hardest-hit areas, according to the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

NONG BUA HING, Thailand—Boonma Klahan starts her mornings by washing, changing and feeding her 85-year-old mother, who has dementia and spends her days on a mattress on the family home’s wooden floor.

She makes breakfast for her 87-year-old father and then rides her motorbike to her job as a health aide to 22 other elderly people in this poor farming village west of Bangkok. Three of Boonma’s charges are bedridden like her mother. Most of the others can no longer leave their homes.

title: Man Arrested in South Yorkshire Over Ann Widdecombe Murder Investigation
subheadline: Haytor, Devon — Police investigating the murder of former British minister and Reform UK spokesperson Ann Widdecombe

bodyContent:
Have arrested a 28-year-old man in South Yorkshire on suspicion of murder, marking a significant development in the high-profile investigation.

Devon and Cornwall Police confirmed that the suspect, described as a white British national, is currently being held in custody after officers carried out the arrest with assistance from Counter Terrorism Policing North East and South Yorkshire Police. Investigators stressed that there is no evidence indicating the killing was linked to terrorism or politically motivated.

Widdecombe, 78, was discovered with serious injuries at her home in Haytor, on the edge of Dartmoor National Park, at approximately 11:40 a.m. BST on Thursday. Detectives believe the fatal attack occurred nearly 24 hours before her body was found.

The latest arrest follows the release of a 26-year-old man who had initially been detained in nearby Newton Abbot. Police confirmed on Saturday that the individual had been eliminated from their inquiries and is no longer considered part of the investigation.

title: British Couple Seriously Injured After Being Trapped in Deadly Spain Wildfires
subheadline: A British couple were rescued from a ravine in Spain's Almería province after becoming trapped in the devastating wildfires that have swept across the region, according to local reports.
cardSummary: The couple, believed to have been hiking when the fire spread rapidly through the area on Thursday, were discovered in critical condition by Civil Guard officer...
bodyContent:
The couple, believed to have been hiking when the fire spread rapidly through the area on Thursday, were discovered in critical condition by Civil Guard officers conducting a search operation near the village of Bédar. Both suffered severe burns and were airlifted to hospital, where they remain in intensive care.

The wildfires have already claimed 12 lives, making them among the deadliest in Spain's recent history. Local authorities have reported that more than 6,600 hectares (16,300 acres) of land have been destroyed. While the identities of those who died have not yet been officially confirmed, reports suggest that four of the victims may have been British nationals.

Dramatic Rescue

The couple were found in the early hours of Friday after rescuers heard faint cries for help coming from a steep ravine.

"As you gain more experience, something inside you tells you, 'Look again, try one more time,'" Civil Guard Sergeant Pedro Barre told Spanish broadcaster TVE.

Following the sound, officers climbed down the hillside and located the pair. Rescue officials said both victims were semi-conscious and had burns covering approximately 40% of their bodies.

"Being able to call out in the condition they were in was a titanic effort," said rescuer Rafael Zea.

Barre added: "We'll never forget the look of surprise and emotion on their faces."

Fire Situation Improving

Emergency services have continued containment and recovery operations across the affected region. On Sunday, Andalusian regional president Juan Manuel Moreno Bonilla announced that the wildfire had been contained and its perimeter secured, allowing authorities to lower the emergency alert level.

title: Jonathan Meléndez: A Brutal Crime That Has Shocked Mexico
subheadline: The murder of the Camilo Séptimo musician, his pregnant wife, their young daughter and a domestic worker has reignited concerns about violence, criminality and insecurity in Mexico.
cardSummary: Mexico's music community has been shaken by the murder of Jonathan Samuel Meléndez Ochoa, known professionally as “Honas,” a 38-year-old keyboardist, composer a...
bodyContent:
Mexico's music community has been shaken by the murder of Jonathan Samuel Meléndez Ochoa, known professionally as “Honas,” a 38-year-old keyboardist, composer and producer and one of the founding members of the alternative band Camilo Séptimo. Meléndez was killed alongside his wife, their three-year-old daughter and a 21-year-old domestic worker inside the family's apartment in Atizapán de Zaragoza, State of Mexico.

The attack occurred on September 1 in the Grand Viure residential complex in the Bosque Esmeralda area. According to the State of Mexico prosecutor's office, the victims were found after neighbors reported screams and possible gunshots. Two of the victims had been restrained, while the victims suffered fatal gunshot wounds. The family's dog was also found dead.

Meléndez's wife, Ana Paola, was pregnant at the time of the attack. Their six-year-old son survived after hiding inside the apartment and was found physically unharmed. The brutality of the crime has generated particular outrage because the victims were apparently targeted inside their own home, in a residential area considered relatively secure.

Investigators have arrested two men in connection with the killings. One of them, Diego Sebastián “N,” was a business associate of Meléndez. Authorities are investigating whether financial disagreements connected to a property-rental business were behind the attack. However, the motive has not yet been definitively established, and the suspects remain legally presumed innocent. Mexican authorities continue investigating the circumstances surrounding the crime. The fact that one suspect allegedly knew Meléndez is particularly significant. Investigators believe that his relationship with the musician may have allowed him to enter the residence without immediately raising suspicion.
author: Mayon

title: Peter Cullen, the Legendary Voice of Optimus Prime and Eeyore, Dies at 85
subheadline: The legendary Canadian voice actor gave life to Optimus Prime, Eeyore and dozens of other memorable characters across a career spanning more than five decades.
cardSummary: For generations of fans, Optimus Prime had a voice. Now, that voice has fallen silent.Peter Cullen, the acclaimed Canadian voice actor best known for portraying...
bodyContent:
For generations of fans, Optimus Prime had a voice. Now, that voice has fallen silent.

Peter Cullen, the acclaimed Canadian voice actor best known for portraying the heroic leader of the Autobots in Transformers, has died at the age of 85. Cullen died on August 26 at his home in Los Angeles, surrounded by his family, according to his agent and family. His cause of death has not been disclosed.

Cullen first became the voice of Optimus Prime in the original 1984 animated Transformers series, establishing the deep, authoritative voice that would become inseparable from the character. He later returned to the role across animated productions, video games and Michael Bay’s live-action Transformers films.

His portrayal of Optimus Prime was more than simply a distinctive voice. Cullen helped shape the character as a leader defined by strength, compassion and responsibility. He drew inspiration for the character's voice from his brother Larry, a Vietnam War veteran and former U.S. Marine.

But Optimus Prime was only one part of Cullen’s extraordinary career.

He was also widely recognized as Eeyore in Disney’s Winnie the Pooh productions, bringing his famously deep voice to the gloomy but beloved donkey. His other credits included KARR in Knight Rider, King Kong in the 1976 film and the vocal effects for the Predator in the 1987 science-fiction action movie.

title: Why Do Hot Springs Really Get Hot? The Solution Begins Far Below Your Feet
subheadline: There is absolutely no heat at the beginning of the bubbling water. On a long, deep detour, it is rainfall.
cardSummary: With no stove or fire in sight, the water rising directly out of the ground and already steaming appears almost miraculous. The true explanation begins far earl...
bodyContent:
With no stove or fire in sight, the water rising directly out of the ground and already steaming appears almost miraculous. The true explanation begins far earlier than most people realize and much below the surface. Before it ever reappears as something you would like to swim in, the majority of hot springs start out as perfectly normal rain or groundwater that seeps through fissures and faults in the Earth's crust, often for years.

What, then, heats it during the process? Depending on the location, there are two primary routes. Groundwater can come into direct touch with shallow pockets of magma, or molten rock that is relatively close to the surface, in areas where volcanism is active. This causes the water to heat up significantly as it goes by. In locations without volcanic activity, heat is generated by something slower and more consistent: the geothermal gradient, which is simply the fact that rock temperature rises as you go deeper beneath. When water seeps far enough, it finally comes into contact with rock that is hot enough to warm it without the need for magma.

The water does not stay down there either way. When heated, it loses density relative to the surrounding cooler water, which causes it to rise through fissures and cracks until it eventually emerges as a hot spring. A hot spring can become a geyser by periodically erupting if the underground plumbing system is precisely constructed to hold pressure until it bursts abruptly.
author: Mayon

title: Venezuela’s Transition Is Moving. But Too Slowly to Solve the Country’s Immediate Problems
subheadline: Judicial reforms, political prisoner releases and economic reopening show real progress, but millions of Venezuelans are still waiting for concrete improvements in their daily lives
cardSummary: Venezuela's post-Maduro transition has produced several important developments in 2026, but the process remains considerably slower than the urgency of the coun...
bodyContent:
Venezuela's post-Maduro transition has produced several important developments in 2026, but the process remains considerably slower than the urgency of the country's problems demands.

The first major achievement has been the opening of formal negotiations between the government of interim President Delcy Rodríguez and part of the opposition. The first round concluded in August with an agreement to begin transforming the judicial system, including the replacement of the Supreme Tribunal's magistrates through a new selection process. The sides also agreed to seek access to Venezuelan reserves frozen in the Bank of England to help finance earthquake reconstruction.

These are significant steps. Venezuela's judiciary has long been criticized for its dependence on the executive, and the Supreme Tribunal validated Nicolás Maduro's disputed 2024 electoral victory. Reforming that institution could therefore become one of the foundations of a future democratic system.

There has also been movement on political prisoners. An amnesty law approved in February facilitated the release of hundreds of detainees, while Rodríguez announced another 131 releases in August. Yet human-rights organizations reported that hundreds remained imprisoned, and many released individuals continued to face restrictions.

title: Alejandro Betancourt: The Controversial Oilman at the Center of Trump’s Venezuela Strategy
subheadline: A businessman investigated for alleged corruption and money laundering has become a key intermediary between Washington and Delcy Rodríguez, raising questions about who is really benefiting from Venezuela’s oil reopening
cardSummary: Venezuela's oil industry is undergoing one of the most dramatic transformations in decades. Under the Trump administration, Washington is pushing to reopen the ...
bodyContent:
Venezuela's oil industry is undergoing one of the most dramatic transformations in decades. Under the Trump administration, Washington is pushing to reopen the country's enormous energy sector to American investment. But at the center of this process is a controversial Venezuelan businessman: Alejandro Betancourt.

Betancourt has become an important intermediary between the Trump administration and the government of Delcy Rodríguez. Former Trump adviser Mauricio Claver-Carone acknowledged that U.S. officials used Betancourt because he understood both the Venezuelan and American oil industries and could connect the two sides. The controversy comes from Betancourt's past.

He became wealthy during the Chávez era through Derwick Associates, a company that obtained billions of dollars in Venezuelan energy contracts. Transparency International previously estimated that Derwick's contracts involved approximately $2.9 billion in alleged overbilling, allegations that Betancourt and the company have denied.

More seriously, Betancourt is currently under investigation in Spain and Switzerland over alleged money laundering, tax fraud and corruption connected to Venezuelan oil operations. Spanish authorities reopened a case in June involving allegations that $42 million in bribes were paid to Venezuelan state-oil officials as part of a scheme involving billions of dollars in currency transactions. Betancourt denies wrongdoing and has never been convicted of a crime. Yet despite these investigations, his influence over Venezuela's oil sector has increased.

title: The Education Legacy That Still Shapes Sri Lankan Children Today
subheadline: Each morning thousands of Sri Lankan children walk into classrooms carrying a chance to their classrooms that was once denied to much of the nation's population. There is a reform behind that opportunity, which is changing the direction of education in Sri Lanka
cardSummary: qwertyuiop(PHOTO: GETTY) Dr. C. W. W. Kannangara, popularly known as the Father of Free Education, was a key figure in the development of Sri Lanka's education ...
bodyContent:
Dr. C. W. W. Kannangara, popularly known as the Father of Free Education, was a key figure in the development of Sri Lanka's education system. His efforts contributed to the development of a system that allows children to be educated regardless of their family's means. The sweeping changes took effect on 1 October 1945.

Kannangara's efforts did not stop at the school fees. The reforms were also designed to increase educational opportunities for children outside the nation's big cities. Central Schools were created in rural regions and talented children from poorer families were able to attend via scholarship and boarding.

A Legacy that can still be seen in Today's Classrooms

How can a reform that’s been in place for over 80 years impact a child in a classroom?

Quite a lot.

A child in a rural family can get an education, take national exams, go to university and become a doctor, engineer, teacher, researcher, or professional, regardless of his or her family's income.

title: What is the reason that some cultures feed their newborns with something sweet?
subheadline: The birth of a baby has been celebrated with rites to express sweetness, blessings and wishes for a healthy life from Islamic Tahneek to birth rituals in Hindu and Sikh faith. Interestingly, modern medicine also uses a form of sugar to help some newborn babies maintain their healthy blood glucose levels
cardSummary: qwer(PHOTO: QWER) One of these traditions is Tahneek, a Muslim ritual that involves rubbing a soft date in the palate (mouth) of the newborn. It is narrated in ...
bodyContent:
One of these traditions is Tahneek, a Muslim ritual that involves rubbing a soft date in the palate (mouth) of the newborn. It is narrated in several hadiths. In the book of Sahih Muslim, it is recorded that the children were brought to the Holy Prophet (Saws) when they were born, he blessed them and performed Tahneek with dates.
The practice is considered as a Sunnah and is followed by Muslim families for centuries. However, there is an interesting question to consider when we examine the concept across other religious traditions. 

Why is it that the idea of giving a baby something sweet is found in multiple cultures?

Within Hindu tradition, a small amount of ghee and honey has been offered to newborns during the ancient Jatakarma birth ceremony, and prayers have been recited to bestow intelligence, long life and other qualities.
Sweetness is also involved in some of the ceremonies of the newborn children for the Sikhs. About the naming ceremony it states that a drop of honey may be given to the baby's mouth and prayers recited and the naming ceremony later held at the gurdwara.

The subject has another interesting link with modern medicine.

Following birth, it is important that newborn infants rapidly make the transition from placental glucose to self-maintenance of blood glucose levels. There is a risk of neonatal hypoglycemia (low blood glucose) in some babies, especially premature babies, low-birth-weight infants, those born to mothers with diabetes.
author: Imaya

title: Solar Train turns sunshine into movement in Argentina.
subheadline: Sunlight is shining more than just on the Andes in the high, plateaus of northern Argentina. It is assisting to power a train that is running through one of the most stunning landscapes in South America.
cardSummary: Solar train turns(PHOTO: GETTY IMAGES) The Tren Solar de la Quebrada is a 42-kilometre long train that traverses the Quebrada de Humahuaca, a UNESCO World Herit...
bodyContent:
The Tren Solar de la Quebrada is a 42-kilometre long train that traverses the Quebrada de Humahuaca, a UNESCO World Heritage listed valley that has been a vital route along the Andes Mountains for thousands of years. The train runs between 6 towns, including Volcán, Purmamarca and Tilcara.

The train's name is misleading as there are no solar panels on the roof. On the contrary, it has to use six lithium batteries to move its two carriages, and solar electricity is produced locally in Jujuy to charge them.

Some energy is also recovered on applying brake the train. That energy is stored in the batteries, and can later be used to assist in powering the train.

The power of a railway in a different way.

So, what is the maximum possible range for a train to be able to run with this?

The batteries have a range of between 100 and 120 kilometres; that's double the length of the 42 kilometre train's current route, the operator said. The train is able to charge at high speed at both Volcán and Purmamarca.
The project is significant for reasons other than technology. In 2024, passenger transport was reintroduced to the Quebrada de Humahuaca with the solar train. The Jujuy government reports that over 90,000 passengers have so far used the service since it opened.

The train also forms part of a broader trend towards cleaner train traffic. Many electric trains use overhead power lines, but battery trains don't require them; they could be useful where there's not enough room to put the power lines up.

The solar train of Argentina is a unique case in which solar power is being used in a different way to suit local requirements. In a region where sunshine is abundant, the same sunlight illuminating the Andes is helping move people through them.

title: Lebanese Journalist Wounded After Strike Hits During Live Broadcast
subheadline: Al-Manar correspondent Ali Chbib and cameraman Mohammad Berjawi were reportedly wounded when a strike hit nearby as they prepared for a live broadcast in southern Lebanon
bodyContent:
A live television report from southern Lebanon was suddenly interrupted when an Israeli strike hit near a journalist preparing to go on air.

Al-Manar correspondent Ali Chbib and cameraman Mohammad Berjawi were wounded in the incident on September 6 in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, a town in southern Lebanon, according to their broadcaster. Video from the channel captured Chbib preparing for the report before a blast struck nearby, sending smoke and debris through the area and cutting the live feed.

The incident came as Israeli strikes continued across southern Lebanon despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire with Hezbollah agreed in June. Israel has continued military operations in parts of southern Lebanon, saying its strikes are aimed at Hezbollah positions and weapons facilities.

The Israeli military said it had carried out strikes in the Nabatieh area after what it described as attacks by Hezbollah involving explosive drones. The military said it targeted Hezbollah fighters and facilities and maintained that it does not intentionally target journalists or other uninvolved people.
author: Imaya

title: US Sailors reach a Thai beach town after 250 Days at Sea and a War They Didn't Sign Up For.
subheadline: The USS Abraham Lincoln departed from San Diego with six-months’ worth of mission time in the Pacific scheduled. Instead, it crashed in Iran and its 5,000-member crew has not come into contact with land for more than eight months.
cardSummary: The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln has arrived off the coast of Thailand in Pattaya, about 250 days since it set sail without stopping a s...
bodyContent:
The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln has arrived off the coast of Thailand in Pattaya, about 250 days since it set sail without stopping a single port—finally, a respite for the ship's crew of nearly 5,000 sailors and Marines. It was supposed to be a routine 6-month assignment across the Pacific and South China Sea for the carrier, which left San Diego last November.

So, what did keep it afloat for nearly 2000 years?

In war, and not that it was used for. The ship was diverted to the Gulf in the wake of US and Israeli military actions against Iran in late February, in which Admiral Cooper says the Lincoln dropped over 1.5 million pounds of weaponry and flew over 10,000 sorties. The situation on board allegedly deteriorated to the point where there were concerns to the Congress about food shortages, broken toilets and mental stress on the crew. The Navy acknowledged the deployment was difficult, but didn't elaborate on the Pattaya stop, citing "operational security".

The earthquakes that struck Venezuela on Wednesday night were a dangerous two-punch combination known as a doublet, collapsing buildings in the capital Caracas and raising fears for the fate of the population in the worst-affected areas.

The first magnitude-7.2 shock struck near the town of San Felipe, west of Caracas. Data from the U.S. Geological Survey suggested it added stress to another nearby fault just over 3 miles away, triggering a larger magnitude-7.5 quake 39 seconds later. It was a relatively shallow, at a depth of 6 miles, and was felt as far away as northern Brazil.

title: Wrong Drug Given During Surgeries Leaves Nashville Patients With Severe Injuries

bodyContent:
At least four patients were harmed after receiving the wrong medication during routine joint replacement surgeries at Ascension Saint Thomas Midtown Hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, on August 14.

According to CBS News and local reports, the patients were supposed to receive medication used for pain control through an epidural. Instead, they were given a potassium-based medication. One patient, 72-year-old Glenda Dorton, was left paralyzed from the chest down, according to her family.

Dorton had gone to the hospital for what was expected to be a routine knee replacement. Her family said the surgery itself went well, but the medication error left her in intensive care as doctors assess whether her condition can improve.

The hospital initially described the incident as an “event” involving four patients. It later confirmed that the medication error occurred in the hospital pharmacy and said the patients received potassium phosphate instead of the intended anesthetic.

The exact circumstances behind the mix-up are still being investigated. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation is now involved, while the hospital has reported the incident to state regulators.

title: Amelia Dimoldenberg Is Closing the Chicken Shop After 12 Years

bodyContent:
One of the internet's most awkward and somehow most successful love stories is coming to an end.

Amelia Dimoldenberg has announced that her hit YouTube series, Chicken Shop Date, will end after 12 years, closing the chapter on a show that transformed uncomfortable silences, deadpan flirting and fried chicken into a global entertainment phenomenon.

Dimoldenberg announced the news in an emotional message shared on social media, telling fans that she felt it was time to leave the long-running series behind and begin something new.

“I feel like it’s now time to move on from this adventure and onto a new one,” she wrote.

For those unfamiliar with the show, Chicken Shop Date was never a typical celebrity interview.

Dimoldenberg would take musicians, actors, athletes and internet personalities on deliberately awkward “dates” inside chicken shops, combining flirting, uncomfortable pauses and hilariously blunt questions. What began as a small project eventually became one of YouTube's most recognizable interview formats.

The series began in 2014, initially featuring figures from the British grime and music scene before growing into an international phenomenon. Over the years, Dimoldenberg sat across the table from some of the biggest names in entertainment, including Andrew Garfield, Billie Eilish, Jennifer Lawrence, Paul McCartney, Sabrina Carpenter, Cher and Cynthia Erivo.

But perhaps the show's biggest strength was that no celebrity could completely escape Amelia's interview style.

Whether she was pretending not to understand something a guest said, awkwardly flirting with them or simply staring into the camera after an uncomfortable answer, Dimoldenberg created a format that felt completely different from traditional talk shows.

Her interviews regularly went viral, turning Chicken Shop Date from a niche online series into a major part of internet pop culture.

Supporters say the measure is intended to address the growing misuse of generative AI, including the creation of sexualized images involving children.

The law officially took effect on August 1, 2026, making Minnesota the first U.S. state to enact such a statewide ban on AI “nudification” technology.

The officer, identified by his surname Bu, was arrested on August 25, 2026, on allegations including dereliction of duty, falsifying official electronic records and obstructing official duties. He has denied the allegations, although police said he later partially admitted to falsely telling the boyfriend of one missing woman that he had contacted her and confirmed she was safe.

The scandal began to unravel after two missing-person cases handled by Bu were found to have been closed prematurely. One involved 37-year-old Jang Mi-ran, who disappeared in May. Police later found a body believed to be hers on August 24, around 104 days after she went missing. Investigators found no call records supporting Bu's claim that he had spoken with her.

title: ‘Frederick Douglass’s American Founding’ and ‘Until the Last Yoke Is Broken’: A Foundational Question
subheadline: Frederick Douglass’s early speeches condemned the U.S. Constitution for embedding slavery in its clauses. Decades later, he saw the document very differently.

bodyContent:
Is the Constitution—the original one of 1787, before the later rights-extending amendments—pro-slavery or antislavery? The question was an urgent one to Americans amid the rising tensions leading up to the Civil War.

As a young abolitionist, Frederick Douglass (1818-95) denounced the Constitution as “nothing more than a compromise with man-stealers, and a cunningly devised complication of falsehoods, calculated to deceive foreign nations into a belief that this is a free country.” By the early 1850s, however, he had reversed himself. Properly interpreted, he declared, the Constitution was “a glorious liberty document.” That startling conversion is the subject of Dennis C. Rasmussen’s “Frederick Douglass’s American Founding,” an engaging, lucid intellectual history. Bradley N. Rebeiro’s “Until the Last Yoke Is Broken” asks the next question: What constitutional theory allowed Douglass to reach so unlikely a conclusion?

bodyContent:
KAMPALA, Uganda—The scariest thing about the Ebola strain ripping through East Africa this year might be rather surprising: It isn’t quite as lethal as those in earlier outbreaks.

Previous variants were more dangerous on the face of it. People quickly fell ill and died during big outbreaks, like those in 2014 and 2018. But because Ebola strains like the Zaire variant were so lethal, they quickly ran out of new people to infect before they could move on to another area. They burned out.

When the U.S. launched its campaign against Iran six months ago, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth promised a quick, decisive blow that would avoid a long entanglement. Now, he is quietly extending troop deployments in a sign that the conflict could drag well into next year, according to people familiar with the matter.

It is part of an open-ended military strategy designed to give President Trump options in the war, the people said. But the deployment of 19 warships, air-defense units, fighter squadrons and paratroopers across the region is straining servicemembers and their families and creating a maintenance backlog that could take years to unwind, the people said.

WASHINGTON—Massachusetts Sen. Ed Markey, who has spent nearly half a century in Congress, easily beat back a Democratic primary challenge Tuesday from Rep. Seth Moulton in a generational fight that focused on Markey’s age and the future of the party.
